title: Markarian 178, marked by massive stars
caption: The blue compact dwarf galaxy Markarian 178, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Markarian 178 · constellation Ursa Major · about 13 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, F. Annibali, S. Hong

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week, December 2025 (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A small blue galaxy with a reddish bright spot near its edge fills this Hubble view. Markarian 178 is a blue compact dwarf galaxy, much smaller than the Milky Way, about 13 million light-years away in Ursa Major, the Great Bear.

Most of it looks blue because it is full of young, hot stars with little dust around them. The reddish region near its edge holds many rare Wolf-Rayet stars: massive stars shedding their outer layers in fierce winds, a phase that comes just before they become black holes or neutron stars and lasts only a few million years.

So many Wolf-Rayet stars mean something set off a burst of star formation recently. The trigger isn’t obvious, because no nearby galaxy could have stirred up the gas. Astronomers think a smaller satellite galaxy did it, hinted at by faint features around Markarian 178 in deep images from the Large Binocular Telescope.
scale: Using the source’s listed field of view (3.27 × 3.23 arcminutes) and its distance of about 13 million light-years, the frame spans roughly 12366 × 12214 light-years. Its light set out about 13 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble’s cameras through seven filters, including narrowband filters for hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur. The color assigned to each filter isn’t published. The caption says glowing hydrogen and oxygen appear red.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the colors are assigned, so the eye would not see this palette.
filters: 657 nm · Optical H-alpha + N II (Hubble WFC3)

explore: Markarian 178 is one of more than 1,500 Markarian galaxies, named for the Armenian astrophysicist Benjamin Markarian, who listed galaxies that were unexpectedly bright in ultraviolet light.
alt: A small, irregular blue galaxy with a bright reddish knot near one edge, against a dark field with distant galaxies.
